upstream_german_metrics.interpretation: Upstream results show a tradeoff rather than monotonic dominance: v2607 reports materially higher German speaker similarity but slightly worse CER than v2602. This must not be generalized to Frankenstein-room quality without reproduction.

source_level_findings: MagpieTTS is a distinct small German-capable expressive TTS family and is not merely another Qwen3-TTS quantization.
The published ready-to-run NeMo-Speech.cpp GGUF path is v2602, while the current model checkpoint is v2607.
Therefore a single label 'MagpieTTS' is insufficient for benchmark provenance: v2602-native-C++ and v2607-current-quality must be represented as separate artifact/runtime cells.
Five fixed speaker identities include multiple male candidates, but upstream source presence does not prove stable Frankenstein male acoustic identity or donor-voice parity.
NeMo-Speech.cpp v0.1.0 is an early first versioned release; API/runtime stability remains an explicit risk.
hypothesis: The v2602 F16 GGUF through NeMo-Speech.cpp may beat heavier expressive TTS candidates on CPU/RSS/startup/TTFA while preserving adequate German quality; v2607 may recover enough speaker quality to justify a conversion/native-runtime path if its extra integration cost is acceptable.
counterhypothesis: Piper/Thorsten remains faster and operationally simpler while Qwen3-TTS or another expressive model sounds materially better; MagpieTTS then occupies no winning point on the actual Frankenstein latency-quality-resource Pareto frontier.
